_comment: THE SEARCH BUDGET (#1135, after the `call` budget, D-1020-D2-6). Down-only: every number here is a ceiling on how long one search call may take, and it may only fall. The promise is the call promise: a member who types into a search box sees an answer inside a frame budget that the typing did not make late, so every search call, whatever its query, is held to the one ceiling. `cargo xtask gate --profile pr`'s `search-budget` step is the gate. The measurement is `cargo test --release --workspace --test search_budget -- --include-ignored`: p95 over 100 calls of each of eleven queries on each of five surfaces, after 10 unmeasured warm-up calls. p95 and not the mean, because a mean hides the case a member notices.

_provenance.hardwareDetail: 4 vCPU / 15 GB, the hosted Linux runner this repository's gate budgets are stated against
_provenance.shape: Handle::call with an AppQuery over the year-3 search vault (centraid_apps_kit::search_corpus::YEAR3_SEARCH: about 45,000 entities, about two million words of Zipf text over 200,000 distinct words, the index built by the vault's own rebuild): Home's vault search and Notes', Docs', Money's and Locker's (unlocked) own, for 2 letters, 3 letters, a common word, a mid word, a rare word, two words, a one-letter word beside a word, a typo, a rare word typed right (the filled pass), an in-word fragment and a word nothing holds
_provenance.seededFrom: Set to 80 ms by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-22 (#1135), after 64 ms the same day: the 50 ms call promise was the first ceiling; after the search-speed pass two cells stayed over it (Docs' two-letter prefix about 61 ms and Notes' in-word fragment about 52 ms on one machine), and on a machine about a fifth slower Docs' two-letter prefix measured 75 to 78 ms and Notes' and Home's in-word fragment up to 68 ms. The owner accepted those p95s and set the ceiling to 80 ms. The ceiling is the promise rather than the observation, so it is not ratcheted down to what a run measured: a ceiling set to the current measurement would fail on the next runner that is one percent slower, which teaches the team to raise budgets.
_provenance.knownFloor: The corpus is a test-build-sized year-3 vault, not the largest one: a member with ten times the photographs has ten times the caption rows. The search door bounds its work by construction (title matches, then the newest 500 others; the correction reads the word list from a cache), and this measures that the bound holds over a vocabulary of 100,000+ words rather than that it is the best any index could do. The numbers are a RELEASE build's (`cargo test --release`), the build the phone runs; a debug build runs the correction pass three to five times slower and is not what the promise is about.
